title: Deliver first-use onboarding and activation for deliver linked screen and diagram editing
summary: Create the smallest trustworthy first-use path from launch or setup to the first meaningful value of `open repository-backed design truth, place screens and diagram objects, select and transform them, connect flows, inspect source context, and save`.
acceptance_criteria: Define the minimum first-use path that leads toward `open repository-backed design truth, place screens and diagram objects, select and transform them, connect flows, inspect source context, and save` without forcing setup that is not needed.
Explain the product's value in the user's language before requesting permissions, accounts, hardware, imports, or payment.
Allow skip, later, cancel, and safe exit where the product can still provide value.
Persist onboarding progress without trapping returning users in partial state.
Distinguish first launch, first value, returning launch, reset, migration, restored purchase, and existing-data scenarios.
Request permissions only at the moment their value is clear and handle denial without dead ends.
Provide a demo, fixture, preview, or sample mode when live data, hardware, or external service is unavailable.
Avoid long carousels, forced tutorials, artificial urgency, or premature monetization.
Teach the smallest interaction needed for immediate value and defer advanced concepts.
Use progressive disclosure for privacy, data, hardware, billing, or safety explanations.
Support accessibility, keyboard or alternative input, Dynamic Type or scaling, contrast, and reduced motion.
Provide complete localized copy and correct locale formatting.
Measure time to first meaningful value and identify avoidable waiting or uncertainty.
Handle network, credential, hardware, data, permission, and external-service failures with recovery.
Prevent duplicate imports, setup actions, notifications, or side effects when onboarding resumes.
Provide a way to restart, review, or correct setup later.
Keep diagnostics privacy-safe and avoid hidden behavioral tracking.
Test fresh install, update, restore, offline, denial, interruption, and corrupted-state paths.
Capture visual or runtime evidence for every critical state.
Update help and support material alongside the flow.
Do not gate safety, data export, recovery, or essential usability behind monetization.
Complete with zero app-owned warnings.

agent_notes: Portfolio Human Validation & Product Launch Wave 13.
Non-scope: do not release, deploy, sign, publish, enable billing or ads, operate hardware, write NAS data, migrate users, merge products, or create future game repositories.
Alternative considered and rejected: relying on internal confidence, green builds, or download counts without observed user or operator value would create false product certainty.
Research, telemetry, and feedback must remain privacy-safe, versioned, and optional where the product role requires it.

Final Wave 14 validity review: `valid-after-sudoku`; publication `publish-as-proposed-backlog`; implementation sequence `after-sudoku`. Human validation remains valuable after the product implementation prerequisites and Sudoku priority.
